title: Temporal-Difference Learning for Dragonchess
abstract: arXiv:2610.01845v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Our research investigates how two adaptive AI methods, evolutionary transfer learning and TD(lambda), perform in the three-dimensional chess environment Dragonchess. The game challenges players with its unique board structure and computational load, making it an ideal setting to study how adaptive methods can update evaluation heuristics in novel environments. In this work we re-implement the Dragonchess engine, changing it from a PyGame engine to C++. This enables faster gameplay, allowing us to run 10,000 games with confidence intervals and significance tests, rather than a single small tournament. Both adaptive methods outperform all other agents in the round-robin tournament. Our results showed that there is no significant difference in the performance between the evolved and learned evaluations. This research establishes the efficacy of adaptive methods in structurally complex, novel game domains.

translated_abstract: 我们的研究考察了两种自适应人工智能方法——进化迁移学习与TD(λ)——在三维棋类环境龙棋中的表现。该游戏以其独特的棋盘结构和计算负荷给棋手带来挑战，使其成为研究自适应方法如何在新颖环境中更新评估启发式函数的理想场景。在本工作中，我们重新实现了龙棋引擎，将其从PyGame引擎改为C++实现。这使得对局运行速度大幅提升，使我们能够进行一万局带置信区间和显著性检验的对局，而不再局限于单一的小型锦标赛。在循环赛中，两种自适应方法的表现均优于所有其他智能体。我们的结果表明，进化得到的评估与通过学习得到的评估之间没有显著的性能差异。本研究确立了自适应方法在结构复杂、新颖的游戏领域中的有效性。
tldr: 通过将龙棋引擎从PyGame移植到C++并进行一万局对局实验，研究发现进化迁移学习与TD(λ)两种自适应方法在三维棋类龙棋中均优于其他智能体，且进化与学习所得评估之间性能无显著差异。
en_tdlr: By porting the Dragonchess engine from PyGame to C++ and running 10,000 games, this study shows that both adaptive methods—evolutionary transfer learning and TD(lambda)—outperform all other agents in Dragonchess, with no significant difference between the evolved and learned evaluations.
